rgb: The scene is an outdoor paved road or cycle path at twilight that curves gently to the left, bordered by low hedges, trees, and tall lit streetlamps on the right and a sloped embankment on the left below an open sky. depth: The monocular depth map depicts an outdoor curved roadway flanked by a low wall and bushes on the right, a raised embankment on the left, and overhead streetlamps spaced roughly within 0.5 to 1.5 metres and 3 to 5 metres below the ground. A cyclist riding a bicycle directly above them starts at the left frame boundary about 3 to 5 metres to the left and slightly ahead of the camera wearer in frame 1 (well outside the camera wearer's arm's reach, while the bicycle handlebars are out of the cyclist's own arm's reach), then moves backward and rightward into the roadway, approaching to roughly 1 to 1.5 metres in frame 3, under 1 metre in frame 4, and within 0.5 metre ahead in frame 5. In frames 1 and 2, the rear half of the cyclist and bicycle are truncated by the left edge of the frame, whereas from frame 3 onward both are fully in view with the cyclist's legs partly occluding the bicycle frame while facing toward the camera wearer and never looking away. Compared to the dark twilight RGB strip, the depth map much more clearly reveals the continuous ground plane gradient, the raised slope on the left, and the silhouettes of the right-side wall, bushes, and lamp posts against the black sky. However, the depth map is unreliable in saturating the cyclist and distant pavement to uniform pure white in frames 3 to 5—obscuring relative depth between the rider, wheels, and road—and in assigning inconsistent relative depths to the thin streetlamp poles and bright light fixtures.
segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates the foreground cyclist (`person` positioned directly below `bicycle`) against an unlabelled black background, tracking them as they move from the left frame edge into the centre-left roadway and approach from about 3–5 metres in frame 1 to within roughly 0.5 metre ahead of the camera wearer in frame 5. Across the 5 frames, the cyclist turns slightly rightward to follow the curve of the road while facing toward the camera wearer (never looking away), with the bicycle remaining 3–5 metres above them and its handlebars out of the cyclist's arm's reach, while the visible elements are within the camera wearer's arm's reach. In frames 1 and 2, both the `person` and `bicycle` masks are heavily clipped by the left image boundary, and across frames 1 to 4 the cyclist's lower body partially occludes the central bicycle frame between the front and rear wheels. The segmentation map separates the boundary between the dark-clothed rider and the dark bicycle frame in frames 1 to 4 much more distinctly than the dimly lit RGB image alone. However, the map is unreliable where it misclassifies the overhead streetlamp at the top-left of frame 1 (roughly within 1 metre and below) as a `frisbee`, fills the spaces between the bicycle wheels and frame as solid blobs in frames 3 and 4, and completely fails to detect the `bicycle` in frame 5 when it is within roughly 0.5 metre.
pose: The body and hand skeleton map is completely blank in frames 1, 2, and 5, detecting a yellow body skeleton for the cyclist only in frames 3 (within roughly 1–1.5 metres ahead and to the left) and 4 (under roughly 1 metre ahead near the centre-left), with no magenta hand skeletons detected in any frame. In frames 3 and 4, the plotted torso, shoulder, hip, and leg keypoints show the cyclist upright below the bicycle, facing forward toward the camera wearer up the curving road and never looking away from the camera, with arms angled backward away from the handlebars outside the cyclist's reach while the visible elements are within the camera wearer's arm's reach. As the cyclist approaches and shifts rightward from frame 3 to frame 4, the projected torso widens horizontally as their orientation turns from an oblique front-right profile to a nearly direct front view, with the left side of the body partially occluded by the torso and bicycle in frame 4. When present in frames 3 and 4, the skeleton makes the exact joint locations of the shoulders, hips, and right knee/ankle much easier to localize than in the silhouetted RGB frames. However, the pose map is highly unreliable overall: it misses the cyclist entirely when partly out of view at the left border in frames 1–2 (at 3–5 metres) and when nearby in frame 5 (within roughly 0.5 metre), omits all hand keypoints, and drops most limb joints in frames 3 and 4.
